def-csm-frontier-dobrushin-matrix:
## Definition

Let $d\geq1$, let $S$ be a finite nonempty set, and put $X=S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with the $\sigma$-algebra generated by finite-coordinate cylinders. A specification on $X$ is a family $\gamma=(\gamma_\Lambda)$ of probability kernels indexed by finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$. It is proper when each kernel leaves every exterior-measurable event fixed, and consistent when $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ for all finite $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$. For $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta)$ for its one-site conditional probability vector on $S$, where $\eta\in S^{\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{i\}}$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on $S$, define their total-variation distance by $\lVert p-q\rVert_{\rm TV}:=\frac12\sum_{s\in S}|p(s)-q(s)|$. The influence coefficient of site $j$ on the conditional law at site $i$ is

$$c^\gamma_{ij}:=\begin{cases}0,&i=j,\\[2pt]\displaystyle\sup_{\substack{\eta,\eta'\in S^{\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{i\}}\\ \eta_k=\eta'_k\ \text{for every }k\notin\{i,j\}}}\lVert\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta)-\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta')\rVert_{\rm TV},&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$

The matrix $C^\gamma=(c^\gamma_{ij})_{i,j\in\mathbb Z^d}$ is the Dobrushin influence matrix of $\gamma$. Its coefficients lie in $[0,1]$; a supremum need not be attained. The Dobrushin row constant is $c_\gamma:=\sup_i\sum_j c^\gamma_{ij}$, with value $+\infty$ allowed. A common uniform finite influence radius $R$ means $c^\gamma_{ij}=0$ whenever $\lVert i-j\rVert_\infty>R$.
lem-csm-frontier-finite-response-covaria:
## Statement

Let $E$ be a finite nonempty set, let $H_0,M,F:E\to\mathbb R$, fix $\beta>0$, and for $t\in\mathbb R$ define $H_t(x):=H_0(x)-tM(x)$, $Z(t):=\sum_{x\in E}e^{-\beta H_t(x)}$, and $\gamma_t(x):=Z(t)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_t(x)}$. For functions $F,M:E\to\mathbb R$, define $\operatorname{Cov}_{\gamma_t}(F,M):=\sum_x\gamma_t(x)F(x)M(x)-(\sum_x\gamma_t(x)F(x))(\sum_x\gamma_t(x)M(x))$. Then $t\mapsto\sum_x\gamma_t(x)F(x)$ is differentiable on $\mathbb R$ and

$$\frac{d}{dt}\sum_{x\in E}\gamma_t(x)F(x)=\beta\operatorname{Cov}_{\gamma_t}(F,M).$$
thm-csm-frontier-dobrushin-comparison:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, let $S$ be a finite nonempty set, and put $X=S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its cylinder-generated Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\gamma$ and $\widetilde\gamma$ be proper consistent finite-range specifications on $X$, each with a uniform finite one-site influence radius. Finite range means that for every finite $\Delta$ and cylinder event $A$, each function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_A\mid\eta)$ and $\eta\mapsto\widetilde\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_A\mid\eta)$ depends on only finitely many exterior coordinates, as in [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. For each $i,j\in\mathbb Z^d$, let $C_{ii}=0$ and let $C_{ij}\geq0$ dominate both Dobrushin coefficients $c^\gamma_{ij}$ and $c^{\widetilde\gamma}_{ij}$ of [[def-csm-frontier-dobrushin-matrix]]. Assume $C_{ij}=0$ whenever $\lVert i-j\rVert_\infty>R$ for some finite integer $R\geq0$ and assume

$$\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}C_{ij}\leq c<1.$$

For each site $i$, define the one-site conditional discrepancy

$$b_i:=\sup_{\eta\in S^{\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{i\}}}\lVert\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta)-\widetilde\gamma_i(\cdot\mid\eta)\rVert_{\rm TV}.$$

Write $C_\Lambda=(C_{ij})_{i,j\in\Lambda}$ and $D^\Lambda:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty C_\Lambda^n$ for finite $\Lambda$, with $C_\Lambda^0$ the identity matrix on $\Lambda$; also write $D_{ij}:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty(C^n)_{ij}$ for the infinite-lattice resolvent entries. These sums are finite entrywise, because every row sum of $C^n$ and $C_\Lambda^n$ is at most $c^n$. A cylinder function is one depending only on the spins in some finite set. For a bounded real cylinder function $f:X\to\mathbb R$, define its oscillation by $\delta_i(f):=\sup_{\sigma,\sigma':\,\sigma_k=\sigma'_k\ (k\ne i)}|f(\sigma)-f(\sigma')|$; only finitely many $\delta_i(f)$ are nonzero.

For every nonempty finite $\Lambda$ containing a finite coordinate set $K_f$ on which $f$ depends, and exterior configurations $\xi,\zeta\in S^{\Lambda^c}$, the corresponding finite-volume Gibbs distributions satisfy

$$|\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\xi)-\widetilde\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\zeta)|\leq\sum_{i\in\Lambda}\delta_i(f)\sum_{k\in\Lambda}D^\Lambda_{ik}\left(b_k+\sum_{j\notin\Lambda}C_{kj}\mathbf1_{\{\xi_j\ne\zeta_j\}}\right).$$

Moreover, each specification has a unique DLR state, denoted $\mu$ and $\widetilde\mu$, and every bounded real cylinder function satisfies

$$|\mu(f)-\widetilde\mu(f)|\leq\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\delta_i(f)\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}D_{ij}b_j.$$

In particular, when $\gamma=\widetilde\gamma$ the comparison bound is zero. The estimates are conditional mathematical consequences of the stated finite-spin specifications and strict row bound.
thm-csm-frontier-high-temperature-suscep:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix $d\geq1$, a finite interaction radius $R\geq0$, $\beta>0$, and symmetric translation-invariant couplings $J_{ij}=J_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ satisfying $J_{ii}=0$, $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ for every $i,j,k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and $J_{ij}=0$ whenever $\lVert i-j\rVert_\infty>R$. Spins take dimensionless values $\{-1,+1\}$; use energy units for $J_{ij}$ and the field $h$, so $\beta$ has inverse-energy units and $\lambda=\beta h$ is dimensionless. For each dimensionless field parameter $\lambda$ in an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, use the finite-volume conditional energy

$$H_{\Lambda,\lambda}(\sigma_\Lambda\mid\eta)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat\sigma_i\widehat\sigma_j-\frac{\lambda}{\beta}\sum_{i\in\Lambda}\sigma_i,$$

where $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ is finite, $\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Lambda^c}$, $\widehat\sigma_i=\sigma_i$ on $\Lambda$ and $\widehat\sigma_i=\eta_i$ outside, and the pair sum runs over unordered pairs with $J_{ij}\ne0$ that meet $\Lambda$. Let $\gamma_\lambda$ be the resulting proper consistent finite-range Gibbs specification on $X=\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z^d}$, as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]] and [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. For its Dobrushin matrix $C(\lambda)$ from [[def-csm-frontier-dobrushin-matrix]], assume the uniform strict row bound

$$0\leq c_*:=\sup_{\lambda\in I}\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}C_{ij}(\lambda)<1.$$

Assume also the common finite radius condition $C_{ij}(\lambda)=0$ whenever $\lVert i-j\rVert_\infty>R$. Let $\mu_\lambda$ be the unique DLR state, let $\sigma_i(\sigma):=\sigma_i$ be the spin coordinate, and define

$$m(\lambda):=\int_X\sigma_0\,d\mu_\lambda,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_\lambda}(\sigma_i,\sigma_j):=\int_X\sigma_i\sigma_j\,d\mu_\lambda-\left(\int_X\sigma_i\,d\mu_\lambda\right)\left(\int_X\sigma_j\,d\mu_\lambda\right).$$

For bounded real $F$, write $\mathbb E_{\mu_\lambda}F:=\int_XF\,d\mu_\lambda$ and $\operatorname{Var}_{\mu_\lambda}(F):=\mathbb E_{\mu_\lambda}[(F-\mathbb E_{\mu_\lambda}F)^2]$. For finite $\Lambda$ and exterior configuration $\eta$, let $\nu_{\Lambda,\lambda}^{\eta}:=\gamma_{\Lambda,\lambda}(\cdot\mid\eta)$; finite-volume expectations, covariance and variance are computed in this law by the same formulas.

Then the following conditional mathematical conclusions hold for every $\lambda\in I$.

1. The correlations are absolutely summable and satisfy

$$\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}|\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_\lambda}(\sigma_0,\sigma_j)|\leq\frac1{1-c_*}.$$

For $R\geq1$ and integer $r\geq1$, their spatial tail satisfies

$$\sum_{\lVert j\rVert_\infty\geq r}|\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_\lambda}(\sigma_0,\sigma_j)|\leq\frac{c_*^{\lceil r/R\rceil}}{1-c_*};$$

when $R=0$, all off-site covariances vanish.

2. The limiting magnetization $m$ is differentiable on $I$ and

$$m'(\lambda)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_\lambda}(\sigma_0,\sigma_j).$$

Here $\lambda=\beta h$ if the energy is written with field term $-h\sum_i\sigma_i$; thus the derivative with respect to $h$ is $\beta$ times the displayed covariance sum. For a finite $\Lambda$ and fixed exterior configuration $\eta$, write $\mathbb E_{\Lambda,\lambda}$, $\operatorname{Cov}_{\Lambda,\lambda}$ and $\operatorname{Var}_{\Lambda,\lambda}$ for expectation, covariance and variance in its finite-volume Gibbs law. The corresponding finite-volume identity is

$$\frac{d}{d\lambda}\,\mathbb E_{\Lambda,\lambda}\!\left[\sum_{i\in\Lambda}\sigma_i\right]=\operatorname{Var}_{\Lambda,\lambda}\!\left(\sum_{i\in\Lambda}\sigma_i\right)=\sum_{i,j\in\Lambda}\operatorname{Cov}_{\Lambda,\lambda}(\sigma_i,\sigma_j).$$

3. For every finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the spatial average $\overline\sigma_\Lambda:=|\Lambda|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\Lambda}\sigma_i$ obeys the variance and Chebyshev bounds

$$\operatorname{Var}_{\mu_\lambda}(\overline\sigma_\Lambda)\leq\frac{1}{(1-c_*)|\Lambda|},\qquad \mu_\lambda\!\left(|\overline\sigma_\Lambda-\mathbb E_{\mu_\lambda}\overline\sigma_\Lambda|\geq\varepsilon\right)\leq\frac{1}{(1-c_*)|\Lambda|\varepsilon^2}\quad(\varepsilon>0).$$

These are summable-correlation and variance concentration conclusions under the strict Dobrushin condition; no exponential concentration, analyticity, or coexistence conclusion is asserted.
